title: Resolve the acting write record from the session's own claim before the default record
action: resolve_write_record (hooks/write_guard/checks.rs:45) falls back to the control-root default record on three arms. Two stay exactly as they are: no session id, and no session record file. The THIRD — a session record that exists but carries no non-empty `lane` — gains one step first. Read this session's own live claims from the control root, map them to their cells' features, and when they name EXACTLY ONE feature whose .bee/lanes/<feature>.json exists and parses with a matching `feature` key, return that merged lane record with source "claim" instead of the default record. Reuse the SAME merge-over-defaults block the bound path already runs (checks.rs:118-145) rather than writing a second copy of it; factor it into one helper both arms call. Every other input still resolves exactly as today. Then the D2 half: when the resolution came from the default record AND the session carried no lane binding, intake_refusal (hooks/write_guard/paths.rs:532) names binding the session to its lane as the remedy, beside the existing FIX line. Prove it red-first: write the failing test that a claim-holding unbound session is refused today, watch it fail, then make it pass.

truths: A session BOUND to a lane resolves exactly as it does today, every typed refusal included — the new arm is unreachable for it.
A session with no lane binding and NO live claim resolves to the default record, byte-identical to today.

A session with no lane binding holding ONE live claim resolves to that cell's feature lane record, source "claim"; a git commit of a source path is then allowed when that lane is non-terminal even though .bee/state.json says idle.
Claims naming two or more DIFFERENT features are ambiguous: the default record answers and no refusal is invented.
A claimed feature whose lane record is missing, corrupt, or names a different feature resolves to the default record — the derived path never emits the bound path's typed refusals.
A claim owned by a different session is never read.
The merge-over-lane-defaults block exists ONCE and both arms call it.
The intake refusal names the session binding as a remedy only when the record came from the default AND the session is unbound.
The new behavior was proven red-first: the failing test existed and failed before the fix.

acceptance: An unbound session holding one live claim is judged against its own feature's lane record at both the write check and the git intake gate; every other input resolves as before; the write_guard suite is green.

trace.outcome: An unbound session's own live claim now resolves the acting write record before the control-root default, and the intake refusal names the session binding as a remedy
deviations: Grouped the new source "claim" with "default" at the msn-21 workspace-ownership check (checks.rs) instead of letting it skip that guard — the claim arm derives WHICH LANE a session works under and says nothing about who owns the checkout, so the sessions that met that guard before this cell must still meet it — found a better route

report.outcome: An unbound session holding exactly one live claim is judged against that cell's feature lane record at both the write check and the git intake gate; every other input resolves as before, and the intake refusal names the session binding as a remedy when the default record answered an unbound session
